collar.wide_note: only where the surround is flat and BoJa approved (Tierra 6, 8, 15)

flush_tool.note: CourseCollarFlush: every collar boundary vertex is pinned to the first other OPCD collider rim_probe_m off the edge (green or blend inside, approach / rough outside), the interior is solved as a membrane (Laplace) between them, so no step at either edge and no lip inside; then every rough/blend/fairway vertex under the collar footprint is sunk sink_under_in_m below it (sink_under_rim_m within sink_rim_band_m of the rim) so nothing pokes through. Collar meshes are the ones whose name contains 'collar' and carry a MeshCollider. Rim = the boundary loops at least rim_loop_min_frac of the longest loop's length (inner and outer ring); shorter loops are seams inside the band and stay free (Tierra 2, 11/3: seam vertices pinned to the proud rough made a 3 cm jump 5 cm inside the rim). The rim probe skips a side where the collar's own collider is still underfoot, and turf in the band outside the rim is capped at rim height minus sink_under_rim_m. The rim pins to the designed surface by class (pin_priority), never to the highest collider: on Tierra 2 the proud rough beside the collar was the highest thing 12 cm off the rim, the rim took its height, the sink then lowered the rough and left the collar 3.4 cm proud again. Green mesh and green blend are never lowered by the sink or the band cap.
flush_tool.conform_note: after the membrane, every collar vertex is capped at the highest designed surface found at its position or conform_probe_m to each side (green mesh, green blend, fairway, tee, apron: never the rough, which is sunk instead). A collar is never proud of the surface it meets; a true maximum rule, applied to every collar, no mesh names.

rim_reset.pass_criterion: every listed pair under checks.edge_survey.max_step_m in mean and fewer than max_rows_over rows over the limit course-wide
rim_reset.note: CourseRimReset: the edge survey's real steps (edge_profiles.py steps.csv, slope removed) are the move demands. For each step whose pair is listed, the collar's major-loop rim vertices within radius_m of the sample move in y by minus the signed step, weighted 1 - d/radius, mean of demands where several reach one vertex; a demand over max_move_m is logged and skipped; no vertex is raised above the designed surface beside it (the flush tool's conform cap); only meshes named collar are edited. Why: the flush pinned the rim to a surface sampled 0.12 m away and then sank the surround under it, so the rim never met what the ball meets; the survey residual at the sample is that quantity directly.

tiers.note: tiers differ in material and physics only, never in height

edge_survey.step_definition: one step_m rise minus the median rise of the slope_window samples either side (slope removed): a bank of 1 cm per 5 cm is slope, a 1 cm jump that its neighbours do not share is a step. Before 2026-11-03 the raw rise was used and every bank over 11 deg failed as a step.

tint.note: on *_<Course> copies per green/blend/collar; milder stayed grey, no-desaturate went neon
